inputs.text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, requiring new registered voters to prove they are U.S. citizens before they can vote in state elections. The official line claims this is limited to new registrants and state races only, yet it's clearly another structural attack aimed at restricting voting access to protect existing power structures. This will fall hardest on immigrants, working people, and communities of color, who already deal with deep-rooted systemic barriers to obtaining the required documents due to historical patterns of exclusion and inequality. These kinds of institutional restrictions prioritize keeping power concentrated rather than expanding democratic rights for the most vulnerable. We need to challenge this head-on to push for real reform and justice.
